title: Learning Rate Schedules
motto: The learning rate is the single most important hyperparameter. Not the architecture. Not the dataset size. Not the activation function. The learning rate. If you tune nothing else, tune this.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: The learning rate is the single most important hyperparameter. Not the architecture. Not the dataset size. Not the activation function. The learning rate. If you tune nothing else, tune this.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Set the learning rate to 0.1. Training diverges -- loss jumps to infinity in 3 steps. Set it to 0.0001. Training crawls -- after 100 epochs, the model has barely moved from random. Set it to 0.01. Training works for 50 epochs, then the loss oscillates around a minimum it can never reach because the steps are too large.

The optimal learning rate is not a constant. It changes during training. Early on, you want large steps to cover ground quickly. Late in training, you want tiny steps to settle into a sharp minimum. The difference between a 90% accurate model and a 95% accurate model is often just the schedule.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Warmup + cosine decay is standard for LLM training. LR controls step size through training.

steps.title: Implement schedule
steps.body: Write the function from scratch in the workspace. Run when ready — all tests must pass.
